reason: The text contains multiple named characters who are not leaders. Most notably, the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah (שִׁפְרָה) and Puah (פּוּעָה) are explicitly named in Exodus 1:15, yet they hold no leadership position—they are workers/midwives. Additionally, Zipporah (צִפֹּרָה), Moses' wife, is named but holds no leadership role. Moses' two sons, Gershom (גֵּרְשֹׁם) and Eliezer (אֱלִיעֶזֶר), are also named but are not portrayed as leaders in this passage. While primary figures like Moses, Aaron, Joshua, Pharaoh, and Jethro are indeed leaders, the statement's universal claim that 'only' named characters are leaders is false.
